children: By Dewi Kurniawati
Malaysian palm oil futures gained in early trade on Tuesday, and looked on track for a second straight session of advance, as crude oil prices continued to rise.
The benchmark palm oil contract (FCPOc3) for November delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange was up 22 ringgit, or 0.45%, at 4,872 ringgit ($1,195.29) a metric ton in early trade.
FUNDAMENTALS

Oil prices rose on Tuesday as concerns over supply disruptions persisted after attacks on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure left the kingdom's East-West pipeline offline and cast doubt on efforts to ease shipping risks in the Gulf.
Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.
Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) dropped 0.91%, while its palm oil contract
shed 0.38%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (BOcv1) were slightly up 0.07%.
Palm oil tracks rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.
The ringgit
, palm's currency of trade, weakened 0.05% against the dollar, making the commodity cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies.
Palm oil may bounce further into the 4,930 ringgit-4,964 ringgit per metric ton, after breaking above a falling trendline, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said.
MARKET NEWS

Asian shares struggled on Tuesday as investors weighed Middle East tensions and calls by industry figures for a slowdown in AI development, while elevated oil prices and higher bond yields added to caution before key central bank meetings in the U.S. and Japan.
